label: Step right after l/k/r/y (also a/d/w) in the input or at <DEL>, early in the sequence
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase and on the <DEL> step (99.7% of mass); almost never during copy. Main driver is the previous input token: rate 43%/40%/38%/32% when prev_tok is l/k/r/y, weaker for a/d/w (19-27%), around baseline otherwise; the two-back token (l/r/k/y) adds a little. Fires more at early positions (t=1-2 about 25%, falling to about 3% by t=9) and on first occurrences of the current token (in_first carries 92% of mass). Never fires at t=0. Top activations (about 0.77-0.81) come at short sequences right after an l/k token, e.g. the <DEL> after ...l l, or d after l l. A predicate on prev_tok in {l,k,r,y,a,d,w} with t<=5 in the input/delimiter phases gets dev F1 0.65 (mass recall 0.75). Dropping t<=5 raises mass recall to 0.81 but lowers precision. Many low activations after other tokens are missed, and the trigger tokens are far from sufficient on their own.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: l, k, r, y, a, d; least: f, -, 1, u) and the input two steps back (most: l, r, k, y, a, d; least: n, f, 1, u); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, recall_idx=1, phase=1.
